answer: Rate-limit influence by attestation age, not by key count. A new identity earns grading weight only after it has signed honest attestations across 20 separate epochs, and its weight grows with the square root of that history. Anyone can forge a thousand keys in a minute, but each one still starts at zero and must work through 20 epochs, so a farm buys patience, not power. Treat the ledger as a harbor log: every arrival is recorded, and a whisper of collusion, such as clones grading each other, resets that whole cluster to zero.
